national-id.options: Bring a PSA birth certificate plus an accepted government photo ID if you have both. PSA also lists supporting documents such as an eligible school ID. If you have only a birth certificate, ask the registration center which fallback documents it can accept.
steps: Check the PSA supporting-document list and find a registration center.
Bring your documents for in-person registration and biometrics. Keep your transaction slip.
When your digital record is available, open national-id.gov.ph or eGovPH and complete facial verification.
Ask a registration center about the paper National ID or track a physical card with PHLPost.
national-id.processing: Digital access is available after PSA makes your record available and you pass verification. PSA gives no universal wait from registration to digital availability here.
national-id.delivery: The paper ID is requested at a registration center. Physical delivery varies. Track it through PHLPost once tracking is available.

postal-id.options: With no photo ID, bring a PSA or local civil registry birth certificate that meets PHLPost’s receipt requirement, plus separate proof of address. With one accepted primary ID, such as National ID, a valid passport or driver’s license, or GSIS or SSS UMID, pair it with separate proof of address. With only a secondary ID, you’ll need another accepted secondary document and one must bear your photo and signature.
steps: Download the form and check which post office captures Postal ID applications.
Bring originals and copies of one primary document or two eligible secondary documents, plus proof of address such as a barangay residency certificate, lease, or accepted bill.
Apply in person, pay the fee and complete photo and biometric capture.
Keep the receipt and confirm the expected delivery or rush pickup date with the branch.
postal-id.processing: PHLPost’s 2026 charter lists same-day and next-working-day rush pickup at select offices subject to their cutoffs.
postal-id.delivery: The charter lists about 24 days in total for regular applications at other post offices, including dispatch and mail delivery. Confirm your route at the counter.

philippine-passport.options: One DFA-accepted ID, such as National ID or an LTO driver’s license, can satisfy the ID requirement alongside the PSA birth certificate. An adult student may use a current school ID plus Certificate of Registration. Check DFA’s format and issuance conditions for Postal ID, voter certification, and other IDs.
steps: Review the DFA adult checklist and accepted IDs for your office.
Book and pay through the official portal. Save your confirmation and application packet.
Appear with your original documents and copies for verification and biometric capture.
Collect the passport on the release date or follow the courier instructions if you selected delivery.
philippine-passport.processing: DFA lists regular processing of 10 working days in NCR and 12 at regional offices. Express is 5 or 7 working days respectively, where available.
philippine-passport.delivery: Courier delivery adds transit time after processing. Use the release date or courier estimate provided for your appointment.

drivers-license.options: Start with an LTO student permit. A National ID or other photo ID can support identity checks. The permit, medical certificate and practical driving course are separate requirements.
steps: Obtain a student permit and hold it for at least one month.
Complete the practical driving course and get an LTO-accredited medical certificate.
Apply at LTO with the required documents and pass the theory and practical tests.
Pay the applicable fees and confirm how the license will be issued.
drivers-license.processing: The one-month permit holding period comes before application. Course, appointment and exam availability add time.
drivers-license.delivery: Confirm card issuance or pickup at your LTO office.

student-permit.options: An accepted government ID can satisfy the identity check. Consult the LTO checklist for alternatives and whether supporting civil registry documents apply.
steps: Complete the 15-hour Theoretical Driving Course and get an accredited medical certificate.
Prepare the application and required proof of identity.
Submit at LTO, pay and collect the permit following the office’s instructions.
student-permit.processing: Timing depends on course scheduling and the LTO office appointment.
student-permit.delivery: Confirm pickup at your LTO office.

local-id.options: If you have one government ID, ask the LGU whether it accepts it alongside separate proof of address. If you have only a school ID or a residency certificate, check the local fallback list.
steps: Look up your city or municipal citizen ID service, or contact your barangay.
Check who qualifies and which identity and residence documents are accepted.
Submit online if the locality offers it, or apply in person.
Follow the office’s verification and collection instructions.
local-id.processing: The local government sets the processing schedule.
local-id.delivery: Ask whether the locality offers a digital ID, pickup or delivery.

school-id.options: Ask your registrar if your enrollment record is enough for issuance. For an adult passport application, pair your current school ID with a Certificate of Registration.
steps: Complete enrollment and confirm your student record.
Check the registrar’s photo, verification and replacement requirements.
Submit the request and collect the ID according to the school’s schedule.
school-id.processing: Depends on enrollment and the school’s issuance schedule.
school-id.delivery: Ask your registrar about pickup or a digital student ID.

tin-id.options: You need a TIN already assigned to you. If you only have a National ID, check BIR’s checklist for your taxpayer category to see what you need to register for a TIN first.
steps: Confirm your existing TIN and the email recorded by BIR.
Enroll in ORUS and follow its Digital TIN ID generation steps.
Upload a compliant photo and save the generated ID.
tin-id.processing: Available digitally after successful account enrollment and generation. Any TIN or email update can add time.
tin-id.delivery: Download from ORUS. A physical TIN card follows a separate BIR process.

philhealth-id.options: Bring one accepted document listed for your membership category, such as National ID or an eligible birth certificate when permitted. Add any employment or dependent documents that apply.
steps: Check whether you already have a PhilHealth number.
Fill in the membership form for registration or an update.
Submit at a PhilHealth office and ask for the ID and Member Data Record.
philhealth-id.processing: The local office can confirm its current turnaround.
philhealth-id.delivery: Ask the branch about release or pickup.

mysss-card.options: Use National ID registration for identity verification. You also need a permanent SS number, matching records, My.SSS access, and approval for the partner bank account.
steps: Check that your SS number is permanent and your records match PhilSys.
In My.SSS, open the MySSS Card service and complete identity verification.
Choose a partner bank and finish its account and card steps.
Wait for bank confirmation of pickup or delivery.
mysss-card.processing: SSS states up to 15 working days in Metro Manila or 20 outside Metro Manila after successful bank account opening.
mysss-card.delivery: The partner bank confirms whether pickup or delivery is available and when.

pagibig-card.options: Pair one Pag-IBIG-accepted ID with your membership ID number and the application form. Check the branch’s partner-bank requirements.
steps: Locate a branch that processes Loyalty Card Plus applications.
Bring the form and supporting documents, then pay the applicable fee.
Complete data capture and get your card or release instructions.
pagibig-card.processing: Branch and partner bank availability determine turnaround.
pagibig-card.delivery: Confirm onsite release or collection with the branch.

gsis-id.options: A government photo ID can support verification, but a GSIS record and eligibility are the starting requirements.
steps: Check your GSIS record and registered details.
Use the GSIS Touch or GSIS office enrollment channel currently provided for the Digital ID.
Follow the account and identity verification prompts to access your ID.
gsis-id.processing: Depends on enrollment and successful verification.
gsis-id.delivery: Digital credential accessed through GSIS. Ask GSIS about legacy card concerns.

pwd-id.options: If you have one accepted national or local ID, bring it with the required disability and residency evidence. NCDA guidance allows a barangay certificate in the absence of a valid ID.
steps: Contact the local PDAO or social welfare office for its disability category checklist.
Gather proof of residence, photos and the required disability documentation.
Submit the application for evaluation and keep the reference or collection details.
pwd-id.processing: Depends on LGU processing and disability documentation review.
pwd-id.delivery: Ask your PDAO about pickup or local delivery options.

solo-parent-id.options: An accepted identity document can help verify who you are. You also need proof of residence and documentation for your solo-parent category.
steps: Contact your local social welfare office or use the LGU’s online service if available.
Gather residence and category evidence and submit the forms.
Complete any required interview or evaluation, then follow the release instructions.
solo-parent-id.processing: Ask the local office for the estimate after it confirms your checklist.
solo-parent-id.delivery: Pickup or digital access depends on the LGU.

prc-id.options: One valid ID can support identification at your appointment. Eligibility still comes from licensure and initial registration requirements.
steps: Confirm that you qualify for initial registration and complete oath-taking where required.
Sign in to LERIS, select Initial Registration and choose an appointment.
Pay, bring the appointment packet and required documents, and follow release instructions.
prc-id.processing: Timing depends on licensing, oath-taking and appointment availability.
prc-id.delivery: Follow your PRC office’s appointment instructions for issuance or collection.

owwa-ecard.options: Have your valid passport and check your OWWA membership and OFW eligibility. Another local ID does not establish OFW status.
steps: Check the e-Card portal’s eligibility rules and verify your membership.
Submit the online application and select an available release option.
Save your reference and follow OWWA’s instructions when notified.
owwa-ecard.processing: Processing depends on membership verification and the receiving office.
owwa-ecard.delivery: Confirm release or pickup arrangements in the official portal.

seafarer-id.options: You need the required seafarer and identity documents for the chosen credential. Check the current MARINA list for any passport or training documents it requires.
steps: Select SID or SRB and review the requirements for first issuance.
Use MARINA’s current appointment channel, submit the information and pay as directed.
Appear with originals for verification and capture, then follow release instructions.
seafarer-id.processing: Depends on the credential, office and appointment availability.
seafarer-id.delivery: Confirm collection or delivery with MARINA for your application.

senior-citizen-id.options: An accepted ID showing age and residence can support the application. Ask OSCA whether it needs separate address evidence. This route applies from age 60.
steps: Contact the OSCA in your city or municipality.
Prepare proof of age, address, photos and the application form required locally.
Submit for verification and follow the LGU’s release instructions.
senior-citizen-id.processing: Processing depends on the local OSCA.
senior-citizen-id.delivery: Check for pickup or locally available digital access.

acr-i-card.options: A passport is the starting identity document for most cases. Bring the immigration and visa documents required for your category.
steps: Identify the applicable Bureau of Immigration application type.
Gather visa, passport and registration materials and file with the appropriate BI office.
Complete clearance, payment and biometrics as directed, then check for release.
acr-i-card.processing: Timing depends on immigration status and the application type.

voter-registration.options: One COMELEC-accepted ID can support voter registration. A barangay certificate, cedula or police clearance is not on the cited registration list for the latest drive.
steps: Confirm the current registration window and your local election office.
Bring accepted proof of identity and appear for registration and biometrics.
If already registered and seeking certification, request it from the appropriate COMELEC office.
voter-registration.processing: Registration depends on the open period and approval. Certification is a separate service.
voter-registration.delivery: Physical Voter’s ID issuance was suspended. Ask COMELEC how certification is released.

birth-certificate.options: Use proof of identity that PSA accepts for your request and release channel. If you have no suitable ID, ask PSA about accepted alternatives or an authorized request.
steps: Choose PSA Serbilis delivery or an appointment at a PSA outlet.
Fill in the certificate details, choose the release option and pay the applicable fee.
Save the reference and check the request status.
Bring the identity or authorization documents required to receive the copy.
birth-certificate.processing: PSA Serbilis publishes estimates by destination and release method. A manual search can add 10–15 working days.
birth-certificate.delivery: Metro Manila standard processing and delivery is about 3–4 working days after payment. Check the destination table for other areas.

barangay-certificates.options: Ask if one accepted photo ID plus a proof of address is enough, and what the barangay can use to verify residence if you have no ID.
steps: Go to your barangay hall and request the specific certificate you need.
Bring the barangay’s requested proof of identity and residence.
For first-time jobseeker certification, ask about the required oath and eligibility checks.
Collect the signed certificate and bring it to the relevant agency.
barangay-certificates.processing: The barangay sets its release schedule.
barangay-certificates.delivery: Ask your barangay about collection. A residency certificate can serve as Postal ID address evidence.

nbi-clearance.options: One ID may be insufficient. NBI’s published general checklist calls for two accepted documents and lists a PSA birth certificate among its examples. Confirm both documents with NBI before your appointment.
steps: Choose the regular portal or the first-time jobseeker portal if eligible.
Book a branch appointment and pay or bring the required jobseeker certification and oath for the waiver.
Bring the required documents for verification and biometric capture.
Collect the clearance or return on the date NBI gives you if additional review is needed.
nbi-clearance.processing: NBI says no-hit cases can be released at the appointment. A hit generally requires 5–10 working days of review.
nbi-clearance.delivery: Check the branch’s instructions for onsite release and any return date.

police-clearance.options: Check whether the current PNP checklist allows one ID or requires a second. If you only have one, confirm any listed supporting-document route with the station before paying.
steps: Register in the National Police Clearance System and select a station and appointment.
Pay or follow the first-time jobseeker waiver instructions if eligible.
Appear with the required documents and payment proof for verification and capture.
Collect the clearance after checks or follow instructions for further verification.
police-clearance.processing: Depends on the appointment and verification result.
police-clearance.delivery: Confirm release with the selected police station.
